security_spec.violation_condition: In QEMU's Smnip interrupt delivery path (riscv_cpu_do_interrupt or a CLIC-specific handler), when the emulated xithreshold CSR is written with iprio[i] — the priority of the specific interrupt being taken — instead of the constant IPRIO (maximum/all-mask-off value), the interrupt threshold is set to mask out interrupts at or below the current interrupt's priority.
security_spec.summary: On interrupt delivery, xithreshold must be set to IPRIO (unmask all priorities), not to iprio[i] (the taken interrupt's priority); using iprio[i] would block higher-priority interrupts from preempting, breaking Smnip fast-preemption guarantees and causing guest interrupt starvation (DoS).

findings.finding: Smnip extension (including xithreshold CSR) is not implemented in this QEMU codebase. No xithreshold variable, CSR definition, or threshold-setting code exists. The interrupt delivery path (riscv_cpu_do_interrupt) handles RNMI (via riscv_do_nmi at line 2242-2246) and standard AIA priority-based interrupts (via riscv_cpu_local_irq_pending), but has no Smnip-specific logic. Since the vulnerable code pattern (xithreshold set to iprio[i] instead of IPRIO constant) cannot exist without an xithreshold implementation, this codebase is not affected by the described vulnerability.

AIA IPRIO constants (IPRIO_MMAXIPRIO=255, IPRIO_IRQ_BITS=8, etc.) are properly defined for priority handling, but no Smnip-specific xithreshold constant or CSR bitmask exists. The IPRIO infrastructure is correctly used only in AIA context (TOP/I, IMSIC, hvictl), not in any Smnip threshold-setting path.

Only RNMI CSRs (mnscratch, mnepc, mncause, mnstatus) are registered and implemented. No mnip, mnxti, or xithreshold CSRs exist. The write_mnstatus handler correctly enforces that MNSTATUS_NMIE can only be cleared by hardware (line 5510), follows proper TLB flush on MNPV change, and uses proper WARL masking. No Smnip CSR definitions are present to audit.
findings.snippet:
/* mnstatus.mnie can only be cleared by hardware. */
    env->mnstatus = (env->mnstatus & MNSTATUS_NMIE) | (val & mask);
